subject: possible bug in geom_bar plot : not sure

messages.author: 634fcb21cb4f65a1
messages.subject: possible bug in geom_bar plot : not sure
parts:
Hey Guys

After a lot of hours and search I am not sure if I am able to figure out the problem here, so for now I am calling it a bug but may be it is something obvious I am missing.  I am trying to plot a percentage bar plot and seeing one variable type ("secondary" : see graph) displayed in pieces. Not sure why this could be happening. Ideally like all other categories I would expect to see the "secondary" category in one bin.


ggplot(data=data_map ) + geom_bar(aes(x=condition,y=count,fill=type),position="fill",stat="identity")


Here is a sample data for one condition

condition replicate      type     count
1       N_0m         A   primary  62204046
2       N_0m         A secondary   7975140
3       N_0m         A   primary  61019168
4       N_0m         A secondary  11333047
73      N_0m         A  unmapped   7291355
91      N_0m         A       raw 142845286


dput(c)
structure(list(condition = structure(c(1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L
), .Label = c("N_0m", "N_10m", "N_1h", "N_24h", "N_2h", "N_30m", 
"N_48h", "N_6h", "N_8h"), class = "factor"), replicate = structure(c(1L, 
1L, 1L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("A", "B"), class = "factor"), 
    type = structure(c(1L, 3L, 1L, 3L, 4L, 2L), .Label = c("primary", 
    "raw", "secondary", "unmapped"), class = "factor"), count = c(62204046L, 
    7975140L, 61019168L, 11333047L, 7291355L, 142845286L)), .Names = c("condition", 
"replicate", "type", "count"), row.names = c(1L, 2L, 3L, 4L, 
73L, 91L), class = "data.frame")

messages.author: 439a20c9d67ff394
messages.subject: Re: possible bug in geom_bar plot : not sure
parts: It's not a bug. You're using stat_identity, which means you are telling ggplot to not do anything at all to your counts. Since you have multiple rows for the secondary category, ggplot faithfully reproduces this in the plot, with multiple segments for each row. I believe what you really want to do is to finish aggregating the counts by type outside of ggplot (using ddply or something similar) and the plot using that completely aggregated data set.
